'''Joseph L. Graves Jr.''' (born 1955) is an American [[Evolutionary biology|evolutionary biologist]] and [[geneticist]]. He is a professor of biological science at [[North Carolina Agricultural and Technical State University]], and a former associate dean for research at the Joint School for Nanoscience and Nanoengineering, which is jointly administered by North Carolina A & T State University and [[UNC Greensboro]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Joseph L. Graves|url=https://www.ncat.edu/employee-bio.php?directoryID=113858234|website=North Carolina Agricultural and Technical State University}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Dr. Joseph L. Graves, Jr.|url=https://evolution.binghamton.edu/evos/seminars/spring-2012/dr-joseph-l-graves-jr/|website=EVOS: Evolutionary Studies Program at Binghamton University}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Dr. Joseph L. Graves Lecture|url=https://aaas.dartmouth.edu/news/2018/01/dr-joseph-l-graves-lecture|website=Dartmouth College|date=4 January 2018 }}</ref>

His past research has included an examination of the [[evolution]] and physiological performance in ''[[Drosophila]]'', a genus of small flies often called fruit flies. His work includes the genomics of adaptation, as well as the response of bacteria to metallic [[nanoparticle]]s. A particular application of this research has been to the evolutionary [[Senescence|theory of aging]].<ref name=":0" />

Drawing upon his background in evolutionary biology and genetics, he has also written two books that address myths and theories of [[Race (human categorization)|race]] in American society. Graves has made appearances in six documentary films on these topics.

He has been a principal investigator on grants from the [[National Institute of Health]], the [[National Science Foundation]] and the Arizona Disease Research Commission, and is a Fellow of the Council of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Joseph L. Graves|url=https://thisviewoflife.com/profile/joseph-l-graves/|website=This View of Life}}</ref><ref name=":1" />

==Early life and education==
Graves was born in 1955 and received his B.A. in [[biology]] from [[Oberlin College]] in 1977 and his PhD from [[Wayne State University]] in 1988.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Joseph L. Graves Jr. (1955 - )|url=https://depts.washington.edu/hservmph/articles/2069|website=University of Washington}}</ref>

Childhood experiences shaped Graves' interest in race and racism: "My parents were poor. They didn't know how to read. I had to teach myself how to read," he says. "The school system of my home was racially biased. When I was in kindergarten teachers wanted to declare me mentally retarded so that I could be placed in a special education curriculum. The regular curriculum had a tracking system," Graves continues. "For no apparent reason, all the black kids ended up in the lower track." But, by graduation day, years later, Graves had risen to be among the highest ranked students at his high school. He accepted an academic scholarship to attend Oberlin College and graduated from there with an [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] in Biology in 1977. His next two years were spent at the Institute for Tropical Disease at the [[University of Massachusetts Lowell|University of Lowell]]. He then earned a National Science Foundation Graduate Fellowship to begin his PhD work at the [[University of Michigan]] in 1979. He completed his PhD in Evolutionary, Environmental, and Systematic Biology at [[Wayne State University]] in 1988. This work afforded him the prestigious President's Postdoctoral Fellowship at the [[University of California, Irvine]] from 1988 to 1990. "Joseph L. Graves Jr. has since used his education to defy racial myths as he has been able to become an important and leading member in the in the field of evolutionary biology."<ref>{{Cite web |title=An NCSE Member Webinar: Joseph L. Graves Jr. on Race, Racism, and Evolutionary Biology {{!}} National Center for Science Education |url=https://ncse.ngo/ncse-member-webinar-joseph-l-graves-jr-race-racism-and-evolutionary-biology |access-date=2026-11-02 |website=ncse.ngo |language=en}}</ref>

==Career==
Graves joined the faculty at the University of California, Irvine in 1990. Afterward he  held positions at the [[University of California, Irvine]]; at the [[Arizona State University at the West campus|West campus of Arizona State University]], with a joint appointment in [[African American Studies]] at the main campus of [[Arizona State University]] in [[Tempe, Arizona|Tempe]]; and as University Core Director at [[Fairleigh Dickinson University]], before finally receiving his joint appointment to [[North Carolina A&T State University|North Carolina A & T State University]] and [[UNC Greensboro]].

===Research===
{{rquote|left|Most Americans still believe that there is some biological legitimacy to our socially constructed racial categories. However, our modern scientific understanding of human genetic diversity flies in the face of all of our social stereotypes.|Joseph L. Graves, Jr.<ref>{{cite web|last=Graves |first=Joseph L |url=http://www.heartland.org/pdf/12721n.pdf |title=The Biological Case Against Race |work=American Outlook |date=January 1, 2002 |accessdate=November 15, 2006 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20061115040049/http://www.heartland.org/pdf/12721n.pdf |archivedate=November 15, 2006 }}</ref>}}

Working with Laurence D. Mueller, Graves found that [[population density]] is an important factor in determining both the immediate chances of survival and the course of [[natural selection]] for small organisms such as fruit flies.<ref>"Population density effects on longevity" ''Genetica'' Volume 91, Numbers 1-3 / February 1993</ref> In "Chance, Development, and Aging", ''Human Biology'' December 2001, Graves wrote that the explanation of individual patterns of [[aging]] must take into account subtle mechanisms such as extensive chance variations in cell number and connections, in cell fates during differentiation, and in physiological patterns that arise during development. Graves has studied the tiny insects for more than a decade in pursuit of greater understanding of [[senescence]], the process of aging.

In addition to the study of aging, Graves is interested in the [[history of science|history]] and [[philosophy of science]] as it relates to the biology of race and racism in western society.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Graves|first=Joseph|title=James Watson's racism is a product of his time -- but that doesn't excuse it|url=https://www.cnn.com/2019/01/15/opinions/james-watson-not-alone-in-racist-thinking-graves/index.html|access-date=2020-07-29|website=CNN|date=15 January 2019 }}</ref> He has received a fair amount of attention from the press for his writings on this topic, especially his strong statements about the socially constructed nature of race.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Science can be used for oppression or liberation|url=http://socialistworker.org/2018/04/11/science-can-be-used-for-oppression-or-liberation|access-date=2020-07-29|website=SocialistWorker.org|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Evolutionary Biologist Puts Agassiz's Views on Race Under Microscope {{!}} News {{!}} The Harvard Crimson|url=https://www.thecrimson.com/article/2016/9/28/agassiz-theories-race-debated/|access-date=2020-07-29|website=www.thecrimson.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=An intelligent argument on race|url=https://www.insidehighered.com/news/2020/01/23/intelligent-argument-race|access-date=2020-07-29|website=www.insidehighered.com|language=en}}</ref> According to his profile on the University of North Carolina Minority Health Project website, he believes: {{blockquote|there are still significant academic and popular views of race that are mired in the [[biological determinism]] of the 19th century and the application of proper scientific method and philosophy, along with quantitative genetics reveals the underlying racist ideology of these programs.<ref name="biopage">[http://www.minority.unc.edu/institute/2002/spkrbios/drgraves.htm Graves profile] at the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill|University of North Carolina]]'s [http://minority.unc.edu/institute/ Minority Health Project]</ref>}}

==Personal life==
Graves in his personal time enjoys playing Chess. He attributes this and much of his scientific interests to his time as a child watching [[Star Trek]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Endowed Biology Professor Graves Named 2024 Genius Award Honoree |url=https://www.ncat.edu/news/2024/05/graves-genius-award.php |access-date=2026-10-28 |website=www.ncat.edu |language=en}}</ref> In addition to his research interests, Graves has also been an active participant in the struggle to protect and improve the teaching of science in the public schools.<ref>[http://www.minority.unc.edu/institute/2006/spkrbios/JosephGraves.cfm Joseph L. Graves, Jr., Ph.D.] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070622203700/http://www.minority.unc.edu/institute/2006/spkrbios/JosephGraves.cfm |date=2007-06-22 }}</ref>
He advocates discussing human biological variation and race in high school and college science curricula.<ref>"Why We Should Teach Our Students about Race." ''Reports of the National Center for Science Education'', v22 n3 p23-26 May–June 2002</ref>
